title: BAD NEWS for Brandon Aiyuk
text: Brandon Aiyuk seems very upset that the 49ers haven't released him. And after being served a warrant for his arrest this past week, the receiver is on a social media spree. He didn't mention the 49ers specifically, but whomever he was upset with, he referred to as {quote} "unquote" "female dogs and little boys." >> They scared. They scared. The truth is they scared. They know how I get. They going to say, "Oh yeah, B.A. B.A. B.A. did this. B.A. did that." B.A. did You know that [ __ ] allegedly. Allegedly. But what they not going to say is B.A. suck at football cuz they know how I get. And they running from that belt that's on the way. It's inevitable. It's coming. Stop running. Stop being a female dog. >> Stop being a female dog. >> Stop being a little cat. >> Being a little cat. >> And stop running from the belt. >> So, here's where we are. It is June 7th. It is unclear if Brandon Aiyuk had expected the 49ers to release him by this point. Maybe he had been on Twitter and he saw some of those erroneous posts predicting that the 49ers would release him on June 2nd. There's never been a reason for the 49ers to release Brandon Aiyuk because they actually financially benefit from keeping him on the roster. He abandoned the team back in November. He's not scheduled to be paid money while he's on the left squad list. So, the 49ers can actually hold Brandon Aiyuk at no financial cost to them, and they can maintain his prorations against the salary cap with the status quo. The 49ers paid Brandon Aiyuk $48.4 million following the 2024 contract agreement. Played only seven games for them before tearing his ACL in 2024. So, the 49ers have paid Brandon Aiyuk more than enough to feel justified and just keeping him on the roster, letting the proration stretch out into the future. Much of that $48.4 million came through signing and option bonus that the 49ers would love to keep stiff-armed past the year 2026, and that's where it's at right now. So, Aiyuk might be upset that the 49ers haven't released him, but that's not the 49ers problem. He stopped showing up to work even after they cave to his contract demands and paid him all that money. So, Aiyuk is seemingly frustrated that the 49ers are in this position of power. Therefore, we have seen an escalation on social media in recent days ever since the arrest warrant news dropped. Now, that came last week, and it's linked to when Brandon Aiyuk sped by Levi's Stadium in a video he himself posted to YouTube back in December. So, Aiyuk himself is to to blame for that, but it appears, based on his social media activity this week, from a racetrack, no less, that he assigns at least some of the blame to the 49ers for getting up in their feelings. Since the racetrack post following the arrest warrant, Brandon Aiyuk has posted a couple pictures of himself wearing a Commanders hat, and now he has posted the video, which probably is complaining that the 49ers have yet to release him. >> We dealing with you know, like them kids when they they don't get picked for the basketball game at the court. But they're the ones that brought the ball. So, they're like, "All right. You don't want to pick me? I'm taking my ball. I'm going home." Ass boys, little ass boys. Or like, when your kid, he got this one toy, but he already know how to use it correctly. So, somebody else about to pick get up and play with it. And they're like, "Oh, yeah, this [ __ ] lit." And they're like, "Wait, wait, wait, wait, wait, hold on, that's my toy." Ass boy, little ass boy. Man, stop running from the belt. The belt coming. >> The obvious implication is that Brandon Aiyuk would like to sign with the Commanders. However, there is no hard evidence that that interest is reciprocal. After all, the Commanders, with their general manager Adam Peters, who has a close relationship with the 49ers front office since he used to work with San Francisco, they've had a chance to trade for Brandon Aiyuk. The window is formally open now. For salary cap purposes, the 49ers would have had to wait until after June 1st, and no trade has been consummated. So, that speaks volumes. Washington, even when Brandon Aiyuk's price would presumably be very low, 49ers would be happy to just offload him for anything they can get. Since a trade has not been consummated, it means that the Commanders are currently not interested in making one. Now, there's a popular misconception that the 49ers will just have to release Brandon Aiyuk before September 1st, because that's when his contract dictates that a 24.9 million-dollar option bonus must be paid out. But, Aiyuk would only be in line to make that money if he actually shows to the team facility and leaves the left squad list and passes a physical, it doesn't appear that Aiyuk is in the mood to do either of those two things. And now he's got a warrant out for his arrest in Santa Clara County. So, even if he did want to show up to the facility to force the 49ers hand, he might get arrested in Santa Clara County because of the misdemeanor speeding charge. It all adds up to being quite the mess. And these actually were Brandon Aiyuk's first verbally spoken public comments in a long, long time. The first one since he was placed on the left squad list by the 49ers toward the end of last season. So, I've been talking so much about, well, we we got to hear Brandon Aiyuk's side of this. We don't know exactly how he feels. We just can speculate based on some of these cryptic social media posts. This one was a whole lot less cryptic. He didn't mention the 49ers by name, but it certainly does appear that he was referring to the San Francisco 49ers. And if we put two and two together, it does seem that he is very frustrated by the fact that they haven't released him. If Brandon Aiyuk's plan was to just get the money and run and just leave the facility and hope that the 49ers would give him free rein, it's clear that that plan is backfiring because teams protect themselves with contractual language. And if you don't just don't show up, a team isn't really compelled to pay you or by extension release you. Perhaps that was the miscalculation by Brandon Aiyuk. It does seem like he still wants to play football. And that was something that was in question up to this post. Now, just a couple weeks ago, we haven't seen Brandon Aiyuk do any football-related activities after posting about his workouts throughout the entirety of the 2024 off-season, you might have expected at least that. That hasn't happened. He did post a shirtless picture of himself the other day, perhaps to broadcast that he's in decent shape, but we've been in the dark as far as Brandon Aiyuk's motivation to play moving forward. Based on this latest Instagram post where he finally broke his silence as far as a verbal statement is concerned, it does appear that Brandon Aiyuk does want to play, but I think that the 49ers are in no mood to give him that free rein because they don't have to. There's one logical way forward for Brandon Aiyuk, and that is to show up at the team facility to put the 49ers feet to the fire and to force a release. And of course, that's a lot more complicated with a warrant out for his arrest in Santa Clara County. I don't know if we've ever seen anything like this, but the article is up on the San Francisco Standard. >> Were you able to determine why he was so upset, why he wasn't showing up, and just any background you can give on that? >> I wish I knew. I >> [snorts] >> Yeah, can't help you there. Sorry. >> a like >> Yeah. >> Has Has there been a line of communication with him? >> There was, but not anymore. >> At what point did that snap? >> Um Well, when I'm coaching, I don't I don't hang out in the training room at at all. Um so I don't see guys much that way. Um But I'd say it officially stopped for me when last time I tried to get a hold of him and couldn't. And then tried a couple more times and still couldn't. And then that matched everyone else that was trying to get a hold of him and couldn't. And eventually there's not much of an explanation cuz it's really hard for us and anyone else to understand. And it's why it's something I've never seen in 22 years of coaching. So just it's unfortunate. And that's it's confusing cuz it's confusing for all of us. So, but it eventually becomes it is what it is and you try as hard as you can to take something that you don't understand. Um but it's not like we understand it very well still. But eventually you understand that it's not going to change and you got to move on with your football team, which is always the most important thing.
